newsitem.title: GERMANY: Exporters' vegetable oil stocks seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Exporters' vegetable oil stocks seen falling.

text.p: A rapid depletion of vegetable oil stocks in the seven leading exporting countries over the last three months was likely to continue at until April, the independent newsletter Oil World said.
Stocks of six key oils were at 4.1 million tonnes on November 1996, then nearly 30 percent up from a year earlier, and were currently estimated at 3.3 million tonnes.
They were forecast at less than three million tonnes on April 1, roughly 100,000 tonnes down from a year earlier.
The six oils under review were soybean, sunflower, rape, palm oil and the two lauric oils.

Oil World said stocks of palm and lauric oils were falling fast in Malaysia and Indonesia, where higher export and domestic demand coincided with lower output while Philippine coconut oil output was down but on the way towards recovery.

A separate study of soya, sun and rape oil stocks showed combined levels may fall to 1.65 million tonnes at end-March, up by just 100,000 tonnes from a year earlier, but down from 1.87 million at end-December and 2.06 million in October.
The report applied to Argentine, Brazilian, U.S. and Canadian stocks, citing lower Latin American soy crushings, lower canola processing in Canada, and higher domestic uses.
